name: AssetOpsBench-CODS2025-Scenarios
description: The 22 evaluation scenarios used in the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench-Live competition, organised into Phase 1 (Development, 11 scenarios) and Phase 2 (Evaluation, 11 scenarios). Scenarios span five functional categories of industrial asset operations: IoT (sensor and metadata retrieval), FMSR (failure-mode and sensor-relation reasoning), TSFM (time-series forecasting capability), WO (work-order querying and bundling), and E2E (end-to-end multi-agent reasoning). Phase 1 and Phase 2 scenarios are paired one-to-one to test agent generalisation across paraphrased variations of the same underlying task; mean inter-phase Sentence-BERT similarity is 0.83 (range 0.55-0.98).
citeAs: @inproceedings{anonymous2026assetopsbench_retrospective, title={Results and Retrospective Analysis of the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench Challenge}, author={Anonymous}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Scenarios were authored by domain experts at IBM Research, drawing on real industrial chiller and HVAC asset telemetry. Each scenario consists of a natural-language utterance posed to an LLM-based multi-agent system and an expected target output. The 22 scenarios released here are a curated subset of the broader AssetOpsBench question bank (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibm-research/AssetOpsBench), selected for the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench-Live competition.
rai:dataCollectionType: Expert-authored evaluation scenarios grounded in real industrial telemetry; no participant or end-user data is included.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No missing values. All 22 scenarios are fully populated across all schema fields.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Scenario utterances are released in their original form as posed during the competition. The pairing structure between development and evaluation scenarios was authored by competition organisers and is documented via the paired_with field in Phase 2 records.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.name: Competition window during which scenarios were used

rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation performed; the dataset has no missing values.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Light text normalisation (whitespace trimming, consistent quotation marks)
JSONL serialisation with one scenario per line
Pairing metadata added to Phase 2 scenarios (paired_with field) to enable generalisation analysis
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each scenario is annotated with: (1) a question ID from the AssetOpsBench question bank, (2) a functional category (IoT, FMSR, TSFM, WO, or E2E), (3) the phase (development or evaluation), and (4) for Phase 2 scenarios, the paired Phase 1 question. Category labels were assigned by the scenario authors at IBM Research based on the underlying task domain.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual expert annotation by competition organisers; no annotation platform required.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Pairing structure was validated by computing Sentence-BERT cosine similarity between paired scenarios; mean similarity is 0.830 (sigma=0.138), confirming deliberately wide variation in paraphrase distance across pairs while preserving underlying task intent.
rai:dataAnnotatorDemographics: Domain experts at IBM Research; no crowd-sourced or external annotators involved.
rai:dataAnnotationPerItemTasks: Each scenario receives five categorical/text annotations: id, category, utterance, phase, and (Phase 2 only) paired_with.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of LLM-based multi-agent systems on industrial asset-operations tasks
Generalisation testing of agentic systems across paraphrased task variants
Retrospective analysis and replication of the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench-Live competition
Benchmark design research on hidden-phase evaluation, scoring stability, and public-vs-hidden alignment
Development of new agentic benchmarks in industrial physical-asset domains
rai:dataBiases: Scenarios are restricted to industrial chiller and HVAC asset domains; coverage of other industrial domains (manufacturing lines, power generation, transportation) is not included
All scenarios reference a small number of specific equipment identifiers (e.g., Chiller 6, CWC04009, MAIN site), which agents may overfit to during iterative development
Functional category coverage is uneven: WO has 3 scenarios per phase while IoT, FMSR, TSFM, and E2E each have 2

Inter-phase semantic similarity varies widely by category (TSFM pairs as low as 0.555; WO pairs as high as 0.984), so per-category generalisation difficulty is heterogeneous and not directly comparable across categories
rai:dataLimitations: Ground-truth answers, full scoring rubrics, and any multimodal evaluation context (sensor time series, work-order tables) are not included in this scenarios-only release; refer to the canonical AssetOpsBench dataset on Hugging Face for the complete records
The 22 scenarios released here are a small evaluation set (11 per phase) and may not provide sufficient statistical power for fine-grained comparisons between agent architectures
Scenarios were authored in English; agent generalisation to other languages is not tested
Scenarios assume access to specific tool interfaces (IoT sensor APIs, work-order databases, time-series forecasting models) that may not be available in all deployment contexts
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Scenarios are released as a frozen snapshot of the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench-Live competition and will be maintained alongside the GitHub repository at https://github.com/IBM/AssetOpsBench. Issues, errata, and questions are accepted via the repository's issue tracker. The canonical AssetOpsBench question bank on Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibm-research/AssetOpsBench) may receive ongoing updates, but this competition snapshot is fixed.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Lowers barriers to research on domain-specific agentic AI in industrial settings by providing a curated, paired-design evaluation benchmark. Trains a community of practitioners and students in agentic-system design for asset-operations domains. Coarse leaderboards interpreted without semantic validation could create misplaced confidence in autonomous maintenance systems; the accompanying retrospective explicitly recommends evaluation transparency, skill-aware subscores, and hidden-phase evaluation to mitigate this risk.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal data is included. Scenarios reference only equipment identifiers (chillers, work orders) and do not contain any personally identifiable information about individuals, customers, or competition participants. All equipment identifiers are synthetic or anonymised representations of industrial assets.

recordSet.name: scenarios_phase1_development
recordSet.description: Development-phase scenarios used during the open competition window (Phase 1). Each record corresponds to one scenario utterance.

field.name: id
field.description: Question identifier from the AssetOpsBench question bank (e.g., Q5, Q204).

field.name: category
field.description: Functional category of the scenario: IoT, FMSR, TSFM, WO, or E2E.

field.name: utterance
field.description: The natural-language scenario prompt presented to the agent.

field.name: phase
field.description: Phase identifier; always 'development' for this record set.

recordSet.name: scenarios_phase2_evaluation
recordSet.description: Evaluation-phase scenarios used during the hidden assessment phase (Phase 2). Each record corresponds to one scenario utterance and includes a paired_with field linking to the corresponding Phase 1 scenario.

field.name: id
field.description: Question identifier from the AssetOpsBench question bank (e.g., Q7, Q411).

field.name: category
field.description: Functional category of the scenario: IoT, FMSR, TSFM, WO, or E2E.

field.name: utterance
field.description: The natural-language scenario prompt presented to the agent.

field.name: phase
field.description: Phase identifier; always 'evaluation' for this record set.
